messages:
maria: quick heads-up — after the 2/12 runtime rollout I started seeing steady mem growth on the kv-cache for longctx workloads. not classic leaks, more like fragmentation + low cross-request reuse.
alex: can you paste profiling snapshots? which metric shows growth?
maria: attaching quick sample from a 30m trace:
```
KV pages: total=128k used=118k free fragments=18%
avg_prefix_reuse_window=1.2s -> used to be ~4.8s
prefix_reuse_rate=21% (before rollout 63%)
mem_growth_1h=+22% on kv allocator
```
sam: hmm. any change to the key format around the rollout? we had a refactor that added session_id into every cache key for easier eviction.
maria: yes — we switched keying to include session id for per-session eviction: `kv_key = f"{tenant}:{session}:{model}:{prefix_fingerprint}"`. thought it would reduce cross-tenant collisions.
kevin: that would explain reuse drop — if session is unique per request, prefix reuse across requests vanishes. did we also change kernel selection/batching behavior? longer batch windows could change prefix lengths seen by cache.
jen: correct — kernel selection change bumped avg sequence length distribution (more padding for short requests) so prefix fingerprints got different cutpoints. combination of session-keying + changed tokenization boundaries -> lots of fragmentation.
alex: security concern: if we drop session from keys to improve reuse, are we at risk of cross-session data leakage?
sam: you can keep tenant in the key to prevent cross-tenant leaks, but remove session for prefix-only entries. e.g. maintain two key namespaces: `prefix:{tenant}:{model}:{prefix_fp}` and `session:{tenant}:{session}:{...}`. prefix namespace is safe as it contains no secret state.
maria: propose we canonicalize prefix keys before writing: trim, normalize whitespace, lowercase, then fingerprint with tenant-salted HMAC. example: `prefix_fp = HMAC(tenant_salt, normalize(tokens[:N]))` — keeps tenant isolation and improves reuse.
kevin: ops-wise, we should add TTL + LFU heuristics on prefix namespace (freq decays) and keep a smaller per-session sticky cache for recent KVs. two-tier approach: global prefix pool + small session delta. reduces cross-request cold starts and bounds mem.
jen: also propose a small experiment: revert session-id-in-key for prefix entries only and run a 5% canary for a day. track: `kv_prefix_hit_rate`, `kv_fragmentation_pct`, `kv_mem_growth_1h`, `lat_p50` and `p99`.
alex: sounds good. also add an explicit flag to the config so Private deployments can opt-in/opt-out (some customers require stricter per-session isolation).
sam: note for Private: we must document that prefix namespace is tenant-salted and not shared across tenants; include KMS-backed salt rotation TODO.
kevin: i'll roll up an A/B plan and safe rollback. timeline: canary 5% -> 15% -> 50% if metrics stable. watch memory and reuse closely.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: created INC-2381: kv-mem-growth-smoke, assigned to @kevin, severity=minor, pager=on-call
maria: thanks — I'll add a short repro (loadgen + longctx) and the changes to the keying PR. putting rough checklist: 1) implement prefix namespace + tenant-salted fp, 2) LFU+TTL on prefix namespace, 3) per-session sticky delta, 4) canary + metrics dashboard, 5) Private opt-out flag, 6) doc + KMS salt rotation note.
jen: one more test idea — synthetic batching change: run with the newer kernel selection but force earlier cutpoints to see if fragmentation is purely from token boundary shifts. helps isolate kernel vs keying.
maria: agreed. I'll post the loadgen commands and sample traces in the PR so reviewers can reproduce. thanks all :thumbsup:
